content: Let me start by reading the autocomplete plan and handoff to understand the full scope.

Let me verify the current test state.
I have the full picture. Let me set up tasks and coordinate the team.

Good. Let me check whether the implementer needs guidance. I'll send them the critical details they need to get the model-alias GREEN right.
Let me also check the Pi source for `resolveCliModel` to verify my guidance is accurate.

Good. `resolveCliModel` confirms what I expected: `cliProvider` is optional, returns `{ model, thinkingLevel?, warning?, error? }`. My guidance to the implementer is accurate.

Let me tell the verifier what to wait for.
Interesting — the implementer's status says "building real-editor tracer RED", suggesting they may have already finished the model-alias GREEN. Let me verify.
All 66 tests pass — the model-alias RED is now GREEN. Let me verify exactly what changed.
Let me check the other file changes.

The implementer's approach is clean — rather than keeping `modelReference`, they eliminated it entirely and normalized `-m` → `"--model"` in `forwardedArgs`. Both spellings now flow through `resolveForwardedOptions` → `resolveCliModel()`. This also handles `--provider` scoping automatically since `--provider openai -m foo` produces `forwardedArgs: ["--provider", "openai", "--model", "foo"]`, which the existing pipeline resolves correctly.

Let me check one thing: the `-m` bare usage error behavior changed from "requires a model name" to the generic "Usage:" error.
Good, the model-alias test is GREEN. Now let me do a thorough review of the changes. I have a few concerns to investigate.

Good — `modelReference` only appears in documentation now, which will be updated in the final verification checkpoint. No lingering production references.

Let me also verify the `--provider -m` combination works correctly through the pipeline.

`--provider openai-codex -m gpt56s do it` produces `forwardedArgs: ["--provider", "openai-codex", "--model", "gpt56s"]`, which is exactly what `resolveForwardedOptions` → `resolveCliModel()` needs to properly scope the model to the provider.

The model-alias implementation is correct and clean. Let me update the task and notify the team.
Now let me also look at what Pi's editor and autocomplete APIs look like, since I'll need to review the editor integration work later.
Good, I've studied the `inline-commands` extension pattern. Let me check on the implementer's progress.
The implementer has created the editor harness and autocomplete test files. Let me check their work.
Good work — the implementer created the editor harness and a RED test for the UI tracer. Let me verify this test fails for the right reason.

The test fails for exactly the right reason: "Autocomplete did not become visible within 500ms". No provider exists for agent command options yet.

Let me check if the implementer is working on making this GREEN and look at what Pi infrastructure they need to hook into.
There's a `getArgumentCompletions` on `RegisteredCommand`. This is the native hook for command argument completion. Let me check how Pi uses it.

Key discovery: Pi's `registerCommand` already supports `getArgumentCompletions` — the native hook for command argument completion. The `/agent` extension doesn't need a custom provider chain; it just needs to implement this callback and wire the `-` trigger.

Let me send the implementer updated guidance for making the tracer GREEN.
The implementer is actively working on the shared scanner. Let me study the Pi autocomplete API more deeply so I can review the integration code effectively.
Wait — I discovered a problem with my `getArgumentCompletions` guidance. Let me check how `applyCompletion` handles the prefix.
I need to correct my earlier guidance — `getArgumentCompletions` won't work for multi-option completions because Pi's `applyCompletion` replaces the entire argument text with the selected value.
Now let me wait for the implementer's progress. Let me check after a bit.
New files: `command-line.ts` and `autocomplete.ts` are created, and `index.ts` is modified. Let me review them.
Substantial progress. Let me check the `runner.ts` and `index.ts` changes and run the tests.
All 67 tests pass — 65 original + model alias + the autocomplete tracer. This is a major milestone. Let me do a thorough code review.
Now let me do a detailed code review and compile any issues found.
All 67 tests pass. Let me compile my code review findings.
Found the issues. Let me send the review.
Let me check back on the implementer's bug fixes.
Bug 2 is fixed (ParsedAgentCommand imported). Bug 1 (ctx.mode) still pending. Let me check back shortly.
The implementer is validating my `ctx.mode` claim. Let me verify it myself — maybe `mode` was recently added to `ExtensionContext`.
Let me verify tests still pass after the import fix and check overall progress.
The implementer has already added the value-chaining RED test. 67 pass + 1 RED. Let me see what it asserts.
The value-chaining test uses `harness.press()` and `harness.waitForRender()` — new methods. Let me check the updated harness.

Good test design — it covers the full chain: type `--thi` → filter to `--thinking <level>` → Tab accepts → trailing space → value menu opens → type `high` → Tab accepts → final cursor position. Let me wait for the implementer to make this GREEN.
All 68 tests pass! The value-chaining RED is now GREEN. Let me review the implementation changes.
The new files are untracked, so gsd can't diff them against the index. Let me read the current versions of the changed files.

Excellent — 68/68 GREEN. The value-chaining implementation is clean: pre/post state analysis on the editor decorator detects when an option-accept transitions to a value position and triggers the value menu. Let me update tasks and guide the next phase.
Let me check on the implementer's progress after a short wait.
The implementer jumped to path completion — 68 pass + 1 RED for path traversal. Let me check the test.
Complex test — guarded quoted slots + filesystem traversal + cursor placement. Let me check the failure details.
Interesting — it passes in isolation but fails when run with other tests. Let me check if it's a race or ordering issue.
All 3 autocomplete tests pass when run alone. Let me run the full suite again to see if the failure is intermittent.
All 69 tests pass! The earlier failure was a timing flake. Let me review the path completion implementation.

Good — `forceFileAutocomplete` is a real method on the editor. 69/69 GREEN. The path completion implementation is solid: guarded quoted slots, directory traversal with cursor inside quotes, file acceptance moving cursor past trailing space.

Let me update tasks and send guidance for the remaining work.
70/70 GREEN. Let me see what was added.
The free-form guarded slot test is added and passing. Let me wait for more negative tests and check again.
Model catalog chaining test added (RED). Let me check its assertion.
Good — harness updated with model support. Let me wait for the implementer to make the model chaining GREEN.
Model chaining is GREEN. Now `--provider` value chaining is RED. Let me keep monitoring.
